title: Socket path /run/user/{uid} hardcoded in 3 binaries; launchd plist ships a macOS daemon that cannot bind it
description:
The same literal socket path is constructed independently in three places:
- personad/src/main.rs:54
- persona/src/main.rs:58
- persona-nmh/src/main.rs:63

each as format!("/run/user/{uid}/persona/workload.sock"). It is the daemon's public contract between the server and both clients, yet it lives in no shared crate — persona-core would be the right home (all three already depend on it). Changing it requires three edits that nothing keeps in sync, and a mismatch silently yields a client that connects to nothing.

Worse, /run/user/{uid} is a Linux systemd/pam_systemd construct that does not exist on macOS. launchd/personal.atwood.persona.plist ships personad as a macOS LaunchAgent, and .github/workflows/ci.yml builds and tests on macos-latest. On macOS the daemon's create_dir_all (persona-grpc/src/server.rs:24) tries to mkdir /run/user/501, which fails on the read-only root volume. The shipped launchd plist therefore cannot work.

Also inconsistent with systemd/personad.socket, which uses '%t/persona/workload.sock' — correct for a user unit today, but a second, independent spelling of the same path.

Fix: one accessor in persona-core that resolves XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (Linux) / a Darwin-appropriate location, used by all three binaries and matched by the unit files.
